When the verse ranking those who strive above those who sit at home came, the blind Ibn Umm Maktum complained, and revelation added the exception for the disabled.
Anas recalls returning from Tabuk, and on a campaign the Prophet said those held back in Medina by an excuse share the reward of every pass and valley crossed.
Ka'b bin Malik tells how he stayed behind from Tabuk without excuse, told the Prophet the truth, was shunned fifty nights with two others, and Allah accepted their repentance.
Some hypocrites stayed behind from the Prophet's campaigns, then made false excuses and oaths, wanting praise for what they had not done, so the verse about them was revealed.
When the blind Ibn Umm Maktum heard the verse ranking strivers above those who sit at home, the exception for the disabled came; Ibn Abbas applied it to Badr.
Repenting for staying behind from Tabuk, Ka'b bin Malik offered all his property for Allah and His Apostle, but the Prophet told him to keep some, as that was better.
